name: Iran nuclear programme
value: IAEA 13 Nov: Isfahan plant location unknown
summary: IAEA report on 13 Nov says it does not know where Iran's Isfahan enrichment plant is; ~440 kg of 60% uranium unverified
state: An IAEA report issued on 13 Nov says the agency does not know the exact location or status of Iran's Isfahan enrichment plant, or whether it holds nuclear material, calling this a serious proliferation concern (Reuters via Al-Monitor). The fate of about 440 kg of 60% enriched uranium remains uncertain and the board meets next week (AFP via Arab News, 13 Nov). Iran's Assembly of Experts called NPT withdrawal an unavoidable necessity, but no withdrawal has been notified (RFE/RL, 13 Nov). No new strike on a nuclear site or evidence of weaponisation was found, so Watch holds.
for_you: No direct effect on the UK public. Developments here tend to move oil prices and the risk of wider strikes in the Gulf; travellers should follow FCDO travel advice for Iran and neighbouring states.
rubric_hit: Watch: inspector access curtailed and 60% enriched stock unverified (IAEA report, 13 Nov); no NPT withdrawal or strike

sources.title: Al-Monitor (Reuters) — IAEA increasingly concerned about Iranian enrichment plant, its report says

why: A nuclear-armed Iran — or strikes to prevent one — could ignite the Gulf and send oil far higher.
drivers: Enrichment levels, IAEA access, Israeli/US military posture, snapback sanctions, talks.

rubric.alert: Strikes on nuclear sites, NPT withdrawal, or evidence of weaponisation.
rubric.watch: Enrichment at ≥ 60% or inspector access curtailed, or credible strike threats.
rubric.normal: IAEA access and active diplomacy; no escalation.
